description: We are very excited about Nasa Space App Challenge.
summary: Outpost Zero is a browser game that lets students run a Moon or Mars outpost and feel the trade-offs behind real space missions. Players get a limited build budget and design an outpost on a grid, choosing solar arrays, batteries, oxygen plants, greenhouses and regolith radiation walls. They predict what will fail first, then launch a 20-sol stress test with lunar nights, Martian dust storms and solar flares. A live chart and a plain-language debrief explain what went wrong and why, so students redesign and try again. Three difficulty levels, shareable challenge codes, star scores and a printable certificate make it easy to use in class. It runs in any browser, with no install or account.
details:
Outpost Zero is a browser game that teaches how engineers balance competing needs on a Moon or Mars outpost. Players get a limited build budget and design an outpost on a grid, choosing solar arrays, batteries, oxygen plants, greenhouses and regolith radiation walls. They predict what will fail first, then launch a 20-sol stress test for a crew of four, with lunar nights, Martian dust storms and solar flares. A chart and a short debrief explain what happened, and players redesign and try again.

Benefit and impact: it makes life support, power, food and radiation shielding tangible for young learners, using only a browser on a school computer or phone. It has three difficulty levels, challenge codes so classmates face identical events and can compare designs, star scores, and a printable mission certificate.

Creativity: instead of managing sliders, students design first, predict, then test, which mirrors how engineers work. Our decisions came from the challenge: key trade-offs, accessibility (keyboard use, visible focus, reduced motion), and simple rules based on NASA resources.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with GitHub for the code and Render for hosting. The game runs locally in the browser and stores nothing on a server. Space facts are simplified from NASA resources and are a teaching model, not a flight-accurate simulation. Take help from Claude for making this project.
